subject: sentences
title: Who, where, what happened
about: The parts of a story: who it is about (characters), where and when it happens (setting), what happened first and last, and what the whole story is about. NC RL.1.3 asks first graders to describe characters, settings and major events, and RL.1.2 to retell a story with its key details and its lesson.
tip: After he answers, have him retell the whole story in three parts: first, then, last.

cards.q: Zoe and her dog ran in the park. They played catch with a stick. Who is the story about?
cards.note: The characters are who the story is about: Zoe and her dog.

cards.q: Grandpa took Ben fishing. Ben caught a tiny fish and let it go. Who is in this story?
cards.note: The characters are the people or animals in the story: Grandpa and Ben.

cards.q: A little mouse lived in an old boot. Each night it nibbled crumbs. Who is the story about?
cards.note: A character can be an animal. This story is about a mouse.

cards.q: Jon fed the goats at the farm. One goat tried to eat his map! Where does the story happen?
cards.note: The setting is where a story happens. At the farm tells us.

cards.q: Mia swam laps at the pool. Then she dried off in the sun. Where is Mia?
cards.note: Where asks about the setting: the pool.

cards.q: The kids lined up for lunch at school. Sam picked the pizza. Where does this story happen?
cards.note: The setting is at school. The words at school tell us.

cards.q: Liv camped in the woods with her dad. They heard an owl hoot. Where did Liv camp?
cards.note: The setting is the woods. Owls live in woods, so that fits.

cards.q: At night, Ben looked up. He saw the full moon and a shooting star. When does this happen?
cards.note: The setting also tells when. At night and the moon tell us.

cards.q: First Ava cracked the eggs. Then she mixed them. Last she cooked them in a pan. What did Ava do first?
cards.note: First, then and last tell the order. Cracked comes first.

cards.q: Max put on his boots. Then he jumped in every puddle. His socks got wet! What happened first?
cards.note: The first sentence tells what happened first.

cards.q: Sam picked an apple. He washed it. Then he took a big bite. What did Sam do first?
cards.note: First asks about the start of the story.

cards.q: The cat climbed a tree. It could not get down. Dad got a ladder and helped it. How does the story end?
cards.note: The end is the last thing that happens: Dad helps the cat down.

cards.q: Jon built a tall tower of blocks. It wobbled. Then it fell with a crash! What happened last?
cards.note: Last asks about the end. The tower fell is the last thing.

cards.q: Ben's ice pop began to drip. He licked it fast. Then it was all gone! What happened at the end?
cards.note: The end is the last sentence: it was all gone.

cards.q: Mia had a birthday party. Her friends came over. They ate cake and played games. What is the story about?
cards.note: The main event is the big thing the whole story is about.

cards.q: Max forgot his snack. Mia gave him half of hers. Max smiled. What is the lesson of the story?
cards.note: A lesson is what a story teaches. Mia shared, and that made Max glad.
